title: SCIM deprovisioning: graceful soft-delete, idempotent retries, and admin recovery flow
creator: Ava Patel
description: Problem: Several customers reported that when their identity provider (IdP) issues SCIM deprovisioning (DELETE or active=false) events for users or groups, our system sometimes: (a) fails to reconcile transient 5xx errors from the IdP webhook delivery, (b) partially deprovisions group membership leaving orphaned role bindings, or (c) permanently removes audit trail context needed for compliance. This ticket defines a robust, idempotent deprovisioning flow with a soft-delete grace window, retry/backoff semantics, dead-letter handling, and admin recovery APIs. Goal: ensure deprovisioning completes reliably within defined SLOs while preserving auditability and enabling operator recovery without manual DB surgery.
background: We already ingest SCIM lifecycle events via the SSO pipeline. Existing behavior treats a SCIM delete as an immediate hard delete of user+bindings. A prior ticket (ENG-4728) improved provisioning retries for create/update but did not cover delete semantics or group membership edge cases. Customers in regulated industries require retention of an explainable deprovision timeline and the ability to reverse erroneous deletions for up to 7 days.
acceptance_criteria: SCIM DELETE or active=false results in a soft-delete marker on user and any affected group-binding rows, not an immediate hard delete

System retries failed downstream reconciliation (e.g., internal role assignment cleanup jobs, external downstream systems) with exponential backoff + jitter and marks failures in a dead-letter queue after configurable attempts
Deprovision operations are idempotent: reprocessing the same SCIM event (same scim_id/scim_timestamp) does not create duplicate or conflicting state changes

Audit logs include structured entries for: deprovision-request-received, deprovision-soft-delete, deprovision-hard-delete, deprovision-recovered, retry-attempt, dead-letter-created, with operator id when actioned in Console

Console admin page exposes 'Pending SCIM Deprovisions' with ability to: view events, re-run reconciliation, postpone hard-delete (extend grace window), and force hard-delete with confirmation. All admin actions produce audit entries
Automated tests covering: duplicate SCIM event replay, partial group membership failures, retry exhaustion leading to DLQ, and admin recovery flow
Metrics and alerts: percentage of deprovision operations resolved within 4 hours >= 99.5%; DLQ growth alert if > 10 failed deprovisions in 1 hour
implementation_plan: DB: add soft_delete metadata columns (soft_deleted_at, soft_delete_reason, scim_event_id) on users and role_bindings; add unique index on scim_event_id for idempotency
API: SCIM consumer to persist incoming event with canonical scim_event_id + source_id; enqueue reconciliation job rather than synchronous hard delete
Worker: implement reconciliation job with exponential backoff (base=1m, cap=1h) and jitter; attempts stored in attempts_count and last_attempted_at; on attempts > 5 move to DLQ
DLQ: new queue table (scim_deprovision_dlq) with payload, failure_reason, backtrace, and link to audit log entry
Console: new admin UI surface to surface pending soft-deletes and DLQ items; actions trigger authenticated admin API endpoints
Audit: extend audit service to emit typed events for SCIM lifecycle and admin operations; include event.actor, event.scim_event_id, event.target_id and pre/post state snapshots
Migration: backfill recent 90 days of SCIM deletions into soft-delete state and emit reconciliation jobs for them
Docs & Support: update SSO/SCIM docs with deprovision semantics and provide guidance for IdP rate-limits and recommended retry windows
technical_decisions: Use soft-delete grace window default 7 days (configurable per-tenant) to balance compliance and operator recovery
Idempotency key = scim_event_id (SCIM 'id' field if present) + tenant_id; if missing, compute sha256(payload+timestamp) but mark as 'derived' key in audit
Retries implemented in worker rather than webhook layer to decouple transient network issues from core request path
DLQ retention policy: 90 days; provide 'export DLQ' in CSV for support escalation
Audit logs stored in immutable append-only store (S3-backed, 7-year retention configurable via enterprise plan)
Admin console actions require 'admin:scim.manage' role in RBAC v2; audit events record admin_session_id
testing_plan: Unit tests: idempotency enforcement, soft-delete flags, worker backoff scheduling logic
Integration tests: simulate IdP 500/timeout responses and assert reconciliation retried and eventually moved to DLQ
E2E staging: connect a test Okta tenant to staging, create >500 deprovision events in quick succession to validate rate-limiting and graceful queueing
Chaos tests: force DB transaction failure during deprovision to validate safe retry semantics
Security review: ensure admin recovery endpoints require RBAC v2 checks and SSO SAML session MFA where configured
monitoring_and_alerting: Metrics: scim_deprovision_received, scim_deprovision_soft_deleted, scim_deprovision_hard_deleted, scim_deprovision_recovered, scim_deprovision_dlq_count, scim_deprovision_retry_attempts
Dashboards: per-tenant view of pending soft-deletes, average time-to-resolve, DLQ backlog
Alerts: SLO breach if >0.5% of deprovisions unresolved after 4 hours; DLQ spike alert >10 in 1h; Fatal downstream job error rate >1%
Runbook: link to runbook for DLQ investigation and customer-facing messaging template
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Soft-delete increases data retention surface for PII - Mitigation: encrypt soft-delete metadata at rest and limit fields retained; allow per-tenant shorter retention via setting

Risk: Large batches of incoming deletes may overwhelm workers - Mitigation: backpressure at ingestion with per-tenant rate caps and token-bucket throttling; burst window and prioritized processing for enterprise tenants
Risk: Idempotency key collisions for derived keys - Mitigation: include event timestamp and tenant_id, detect collisions and surface to DLQ for manual review
Risk: Admin misuse of 'force hard-delete' - Mitigation: require two-step confirmation, record admin session and justification in audit, and restrict to 'platform-admin' role
open_questions: Should soft-deleted users continue to be excluded from billing immediately or only after hard-delete? Prefer immediate exclusion but confirm with finance
What's the default per-tenant max retry attempts? Current plan is 5 but opt-in enterprise customers may want configurable up to 10
How do we surface linked downstream systems that also must be notified (e.g., internal analytics) to avoid eventual inconsistency? Need a mapping table and outbound hooks
notes: Related ticket: ENG-4728 improved provisioning retries on create/update; reuse worker/backoff primitives from that change
GitHub: PR notes and WIP branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/12456
